elements.element: Customer is subject to no non-compete restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4 is reserved, eliminating the former non-compete, while Section 12.3 expressly confirms that Customer made no non-compete commitment and remains free to develop, acquire, license, sell, or use any product or service.

elements.element: Customer is subject to no field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly permits Customer to conduct business in any field or territory.

elements.element: Any restriction is limited to a specifically named competing product.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains: Section 12.4 is reserved and Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves Customer's freedom regarding any product or service. The condition for limiting an operative restriction to a named product is therefore demonstrably absent.

elements.element: Any restriction applies only during the term.
elements.evidence: No restriction applies during or after the term because Section 12.4 is reserved and Section 12.3 confirms no non-compete commitment.

elements.element: Any restriction is capped at 12 months.
elements.evidence: No restriction remains, so its effective duration is zero and does not exceed 12 months.

elements.element: Any restriction carves out Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service, which encompasses internal development.

elements.element: Any restriction carves out Customer's acquisitions.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3 expressly states that nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service.

result.reason: The operative redline fully achieves the preferred position by deleting the non-compete and retaining express protections against non-compete and field-of-use restrictions. It necessarily also meets the fallback's narrower limits. Reserving Section 12.4 is a minimal, clear edit that removes the conflicting restriction without altering unrelated commercial terms.
